Commentary.Commentary: West Indies have a revised DLS target. They need 181 RUNS TO WIN IN 35 OVERS. Back for the chase. Evin Lewis and Brandon King to open for West Indies. Shaheen Afridi to steam in first.
...THE CHASE...

Update - 7.26 pm GMT - The covers are coming off! Nice and bright right now. PAKISTAN'S INNINGS COME TO AN END WITH THAT. So, a start-and-stop kind of play and it hasn't helped Pakistan at all. However, take nothing away from the relentless bowling pressure from West Indies which have helped them keep Pakistan at bay. The pacers were just as good as they could under overcast conditions and never allowed Pakistan to build any kind of partnership. West Indies now have a big chance to level the series but will hope tha rain stays away from hereon.

UPDATE - 6.05 pm GMT- Well, some good news as the live visuals show that the rain has stopped but the covers are still firmly on. The supper-soppers are working and the drainage here is fantastic, so it should not take that long. Stick with us for further news.

UPDATE - 5.56 pm GMT - Unfortunately, it is still raining heavily and with every minute passing, it is looking unlikely that Pakistan will bat again. However, West Indies will be hoping that at least this game happens even if it is a shortened one as they are well positioned to force a decider.

UPDATE - 5.33 pm GMT - No new word from the ground, as it is still raining. Well, now we can surely say that when the match restarts, if it does, we will definitely lose overs, as we have consumed the buffer time fully.

Just what we did not want! The drizzle has picked up and arrived at the ground now. The umpire thinks that it is enough to ask for the covers again. We can see the West Indies players reluctantly leaving the field as the momentum was with them, but no one can control the weather. We are in for another delay here. Hopefully, it is not a long one. OUT! LBW! Gudakesh Motie strikes! He gets a huge wicket here and the Windies will feel they are on top here now. Tossed up, full and on middle and leg, turns away a shy bit. Mohammad Rizwan goes down to sweep it away, but makes a meal of it and misses. The ball turns past his bat and hits him on the pads. There is a big shout for LBW, and after taking his time, the umpire raises his finger. However, Rizwan takes the review here. UltraEdge confirms no bat involved and Ball Tracking comes up with two reds and wickets umpire's call as the ball is just hitting the top of off. Rizwan is not happy, but nothing can be done now. Pakistan keep the review but lose their skipper, who goes back for a struggling 16 off 38, and never looked like going.

UPDATE - Positive news coming from the ground! The rain has stopped again, and the covers are coming off, too. We also have resumption time - 3.50 PM GMT. This is also just before the buffer time expires, so no overs are being lost.

UPDATE - 3.31 pm GMT - Oh..no! Just when we were about to restart, the drizzle is back on. The umpires ask for the covers to be put back on. While writing this, the rain has gotten even heavier, and we are in for another break here. Now, it increasingly looks like, if and when we get going, we will be losing overs, as 40 minutes or so of the buffer time has already gone. Fingers crossed for now!

UPDATE - 3.13 pm GMT - Good news, folks! The rain has stopped, and the visuals show that the sun is out and the covers are being removed now. We can see the dryers and super-soppers all in action. The word from the middle is that the MATCH WILL RESUME AT 3.30 PM GMT, barring further rain. We are not expected to lose any overs, as we have an hour of buffer time.

Uh..oh! As the forecast predicted, the rain has arrived in Trinidad and Tobago. The umpires give the marching orders to the players as they quickly make their way off the field, while the groundsmen come in with the covers. They put the hessian on the pitch and the blue covers on top of that. Hopefully, this is just a passing shower, and we can get going as soon as possible. Stay tuned for more updates.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The conditions at the moment are clear, but there is forecast of some rain, but we hope that it stays away. We can see the two umpires make their way out to the middle now, followed by the West Indies players. They take up their respective field positions. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique are the two openers for Pakistan. Jayden Seales has the new ball in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Babar Azam of Pakistan also share a few words. He says that he loves playing against West Indies because they are a good team and has a lot of quality bowlers. Adds that it is different conditions for him, as he is playing here for the first time, and it is challenging. Tells that it is two-paced and the ball was coming a bit slow as well. Mentions that assessing the conditions is key, and according to him, the top order needs to take more responsibility, and someone from there needs to stay till the end.

Ravi Rampaul, the bowling coach of West Indies, is up for a quick chat. He says that a lot of work has to be done in the bowling unit. Adds that they lack consistency in the white-ball formats and change players often. Mentions that it is important to pick up a few early wickets, and then a couple in the middle makes the backend easier. Says that the all-round ability in the team helps, but they need to attack more with the ball and stick to certain areas.

PITCH REPORT - Carlos Brathwaite is pitchside. He says that the sun is shining brightly at the moment, but he is not sure how long that will last. Adds that the square boundaries are 64 and 62 meters, while the straight hit is 74 meters. Stacy Ann King joins him and says that there might be some rain later on, but the surface feels warm, and the seamers will get movement early on. Ends by saying that the spinners will need to find the right line and length, while the batters will have to be patient, and the team that bats better will win.

Mohammad Rizwan, the captain of Pakistan, says that they wanted to bat first, but the toss does not matter that much. Adds that now they have to be ready to put a good total on the board. Praises Hasan Nawaz for the way he has been performing and says he was doing this in the PSL, and it is good that he is able to continue at the international stage as well. Informs they have made three changes as Mohammad Nawaz, Hasan Ali, and Abrar Ahmed come in the team.

Shai Hope, the skipper of West Indies, says that he wants to bowl first because there is some moisture on the surface and a bit of rain around as well. Adds that they cannot be too specific about where they need to improve, as he thinks they need a collective performance. Mentions that batting has let them down, and they want to do better here. Says that they have been one of the best scoring teams in the middle overs playing spin, and he just wants their batters to remember that. He hopes they can put up a good score and put pressure on Pakistan in the chase. Informs that Romario Shepherd is resting, and Justin Greaves comes in for him.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abdullah Shafique, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan (C/WK), Salman Agha, Hasan Nawaz, Hussain Talat, Mohammad Nawaz (In place of Faheem Ashraf), Shaheen Afridi, Hasan Ali (In place of Naseem Shah), Abrar Ahmed (In place of Sufiyan Muqeem).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Evin Lewis, Keacy Carty, Shai Hope (C/WK), Sherfane Rutherford, Justin Greaves (In place of Romario Shepherd), Gudakesh Motie, Roston Chase, Shamar Joseph, Jayden Seales, Jediah Blades.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Shai Hope and West Indies have elected to BOWL first.

West Indies find themselves in a tough spot, struggling to notch up wins across formats. While a few individuals have shone, the all-important collective performance remains elusive. Skipper Shai Hope continues to shoulder the batting responsibilities with composure, and though Evin Lewis and Roston Chase offered some resistance in the last game, consistency has been their Achilles’ heel. The bowling unit, too, looked a touch off the mark, but the Windies will bank on the fiery Shamar Joseph to spark something special, with Jayden Seales and Gudakesh Motie expected to back him up in applying pressure. With pride on the line and the series at stake, the hosts will be desperate to produce a spirited display, level the series, and give their fans a much-needed reason to cheer. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Pakistan made light work of a target close to 300 in the series opener, with the seasoned duo of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan anchoring the chase. But it was the young sensation Hasan Nawaz who truly lit up the evening, smashing a classy unbeaten half-century that stole the limelight. Backed by several in-form batters raring to go, this Pakistan side looks a well-oiled machine. While their spinners ruled the roost in the T20Is, the spotlight in ODIs shifts to their fearsome pace pair of Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah, who can rattle any batting lineup with their swing, pace, and aggression. Riding high on confidence and momentum, the Men in Green will be determined to wrap things up here and avoid the tension of a series decider.

Hello and a very warm welcome, folks! We’re back at the vibrant Brian Lara Cricket Academy for what promises to be another cracking contest - the 2nd ODI between West Indies and Pakistan. The Men in Green arrive with their tails up, leading the series 1-0 and eyeing a clinical finish to seal the deal. But make no mistake, the hosts are hurting. After coming up short in the T20Is and now staring down the barrel in the ODIs, the Windies know they can’t afford another slip.
... MATCH DAY ...

After falling behind 1-0 in the series, the West Indies face a crucial quick turnaround as they take on Pakistan in the second ODI at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba. In the first match, the hosts posted 280 runs thanks to half-centuries from Evin Lewis, Shai Hope, and Roston Chase, though the total seemed slightly below par at the halfway mark. With the ball, West Indies managed to break key partnerships, reducing Pakistan to 180 for 5. However, debutant Hasan Nawaz, alongside Hussain Talat, steered the visitors home with an unbeaten 104-run partnership. Squandered starts marked the home side’s innings, and much of the responsibility now lies with their top four of Brandon King, Evin Lewis, Keacy Carty, and Shai Hope to lay the foundation for the power hitters down the order. Even Pakistan experienced a similar issue, with batters failing to convert starts into big scores. Saim Ayub, in particular, had little impact, and his side will be relying on him to provide the brisk starts he is known for. The toss played a crucial role in the first ODI, as the surface was noticeably slower during the first innings. As the game progressed into the night, conditions improved for the batters with the presence of dew creating challenges for the Windies' spinners. For the upcoming second ODI, a day game, the pitch is likely to become slower as the match progresses. West Indies are yet to win a series in this home season, having faced defeats in both Tests and T20Is against Australia, and then a 2-1 loss to Pakistan in the T20I series before the ODIs. Can Shai Hope and Co. click as a unit and take the series to a decider? We shall find out.
